title: Capacity & queue scratchlist
content:
Quick brain dump for the day — personal checklist + todo, messy.

MOTIVATION: keep queue moving, free up capacity for nightly batches, avoid preempt storms.

Today 09:10 — snapshot of pools:
- gpu-pool-x86 (pfast): 24 nodes, 88% avg utilization last 12h, 3 nodes in pending (OOM on cuda driver upgrade)
- gpu-pool-arm (quant): 8 nodes, 45% util, safe headroom 3 nodes
- gpu-burst: 6 nodes, 95% spikes nightly 00:00-03:00

Immediate actions (top of mind)
- [ ] Reclaim stale jobs in queue-ml-urgent (older than 6h) — use cancel-old.sh (see snippet)
- [ ] Patch nodes with driver 525 -> 535 on pfast; coordinate with SRE window 13:00-14:00
- [ ] Disable auto-burst on gpu-burst for next 24h until we root cause preemptions
- [ ] Add temporary quota bump for experiment/llm-finetune team: +2 gpus (track chargeback)

Commands I keep forgetting (put here so I don’t open history):
- cancel-old.sh --queue queue-ml-urgent --age 6h --dry-run
- ./node-health-check --pool gpu-pool-x86 --nvml-check --collect-logs /tmp/nvml-$(date +%s).tgz
- kubectl cordon node/gpu-x86-24 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Notes from 10:45 triage with Samir:
- OOMs: likely caused by kernel+driver mismatch after recent security patch. Repro: run warmup workload -> KV cache gets stuck -> container still shows memory reserved by nvidia-container-toolkit.
- Next step: boot 1 canary node, run warmup script, monitor nvml + dmesg. If OK, rolling patch 3 nodes at a time.

Longer running items (not urgent but weekly):
- Right-size pooling policy for batch-inference routes (cost vs latency). Gather 7d p95 latency and cost per token.
- Evaluate quant-pool utilization to see if we can collapse small instances into one AZ to reduce cross-AZ egress.
- Finish doc for GPU maintenance window template (draft in Confluence).

Backfill / handoff notes for next shift (if I get pulled):
- If bursts keep preempting, flip feature flag: infra.burst.disable until 03/15.
- Look at /metrics/infra/gpu/retries — if > 100/hr escalate to SRE on-call.
- Handoff: left canary node gpu-x86-canary-1 patched and repro run started (logs -> /var/tmp/canary-logs.tgz).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Can we reduce default container shared memory for finetune images from 16G -> 8G without breaking experiments? quick A/B test needed.
- Who owns quota approval for ad-hoc research bumps? need formal flow (maybe a GitHub issue template + finance tag).
- Is the burst autoscaler respecting topologySpread constraints? observed 2 pods scheduled same rack -> network saturation.

Small TODOs I will try to finish before EOD:
- [ ] Run canary repro script (target 11:30)
- [ ] Post update to #infra-gpu with summary and next steps
- [ ] Open follow-up Jira for driver-patch rollback plan if canary fails
- [ ] Ping Leah about capacity forecast numbers for next sprint

Random references + links I paste often (so they live here):
- driver rollback runbook: confluence.redwood/infra/driver-rollback
- warmup script: https://git/redwood/scripts/gpu-warmup.sh
- chargeback spreadsheet: drive.redwood/sheets/gpu-chargeback-2026

Tidy-up ideas (meta):
- Keep a one-liner status pinned to each pool (like pfast:short-upd) so triage is faster
- Build quick dashboard tile: "queue age > 4h" with jump-to-cancel button (ask frontend for MVP)

End of dump. Will refine into a cleaned list if I have spare 30m.

-- Riley
notes: messy and intentionally skeletal, meant to be ephemeral.
